## CURRENT ARCHITECTURE

- One browser PWA for desktop and mobile, using the existing HTTPS JSON API with its name and endpoints preserved.
- Separate, replaceable **LocalStore** and **SyncEngine** boundaries; screens access persistence through LocalStore.
- LocalStore uses IndexedDB for inspection records. Its attachment adapter prefers filesystem storage when supported and authorized, otherwise uses IndexedDB blobs through one read/write/delete contract.
- PostgreSQL stores inspection identity and version state. A stable client UUID provides create idempotency; the server ID and last acknowledged version are retained locally. Update version checks independently reject stale edits.
- SyncEngine is resumable and starts on app launch, pull to refresh, or an online local edit.

## CURRENT CONSTRAINTS

- Retain drafts and photos until authenticated upload completion is acknowledged **for that item**. Timeouts, expired sessions, validation failures, lost responses, and successful uploads of unrelated items never authorize cleanup.
- Persist acknowledged transfer progress per attachment; partial chunk success is not full completion. Resume after interruption, or safely restart an unsupported resumable transfer using its stable attachment identifier.
- Retry transient network/service failures with capped exponential backoff and jitter. Validation requires correction; conflicts require explicit review without automatic narrative merging; expired authentication waits for reauthentication.
- Preserve record-before-attachment ordering while allowing independent valid queue items to continue.
- Adapter writes return persisted references only after storage succeeds; reads return original bytes and metadata; deletes affect only the specified reference. SyncEngine owns upload acknowledgement and cleanup decisions.
- Permission denial uses blob fallback. Quota or transaction failures must produce actionable errors, retain working form state in memory, and never claim durability before commit. Partial writes must not report success with missing bytes; the specific error-versus-fallback policy is not settled in the supplied conversation.
- Use plain UTF-8 text with required-field and maximum-length validation. Provide readable, screen-reader-accessible status and meaningful state announcements, without announcing every retry.
- Exclude admin dashboards, analytics/reporting, push notifications, background periodic sync, and rich text. Visual backlog, localization notes, and unconfirmed pilot scheduling do not change this engineering scope.

## SUPERSEDED DECISIONS

- Native desktop client and desktop-wrapper fallback → one browser PWA.
- localStorage production persistence → IndexedDB records.
- Filesystem-only attachments → capability- and permission-aware filesystem preference with IndexedDB blob fallback.
- WebSocket push, including the later optional proposal → the three agreed foreground sync triggers.
- Proposed API rename → preserve the established service name and endpoints.

## CURRENT STATE

The PWA shell and record form are implemented. IndexedDB record persistence and offline reload recovery are integrated with metadata synchronization, UUID replay handling, acknowledged-version storage, and validation/conflict pauses. Existing checks cover create replay, stale-update rejection, server-row preservation, draft recovery, and conflict display without clearing local content.

Attachments remain unfinished: photos use a temporary test-harness path, the shared interface is drafted, and neither production backend has passed the common contract suite. End-to-end attachment transfer and cleanup are incomplete.

## NEXT STEP

Complete LocalStore attachment backend selection and both read/write/delete implementations. Run shared tests for byte/metadata fidelity, identifier association, reload persistence, permission fallback, storage failures, and acknowledgement-gated cleanup. Verify capability and permission behavior on representative browsers.

After those tests pass, connect the adapter to SyncEngine and validate interrupted transfers, expired authentication, lost responses, and cleanup limited to the acknowledged attachment. Keep this work scoped to the existing API and attachment path.
